config.title: FUNDA — Smart Truncate Pipe

intro.title: FUNDA — Smart Truncate Pipe
intro.body: In this lesson you will build a Smart Truncate Pipe — a configurable pure pipe that shortens long text strings to a specified character limit and appends a customisable suffix (e.g., "…" or "read more"). You will then extend it into an impure variant that reacts to window resize events, truncating to a shorter limit on mobile viewports. By building both variants you will deeply understand what pure and impure mean in Angular's change detection context.
intro.usecase: Pipes are Angular's built-in memoisation for templates: pure pipes re-run only when their input reference changes. Custom pipes appear in news feeds, product catalogues, notification lists, and dashboards.

objectives: Implement a pure TruncatePipe with configurable limit and trail parameters using the PipeTransform interface
Explain why a pure pipe is only re-evaluated when its input reference changes, and how this provides automatic memoisation
Demonstrate that replacing a pipe with an equivalent template method call causes that method to execute on every CD cycle
Extend the pipe to an impure variant (pure: false) and inject the current viewport width via a breakpoint service
Articulate the performance implications of impure pipes and identify when they are justified versus when a computed Signal is superior
Register the pipe as standalone and use it in multiple components without importing CommonModule
Write unit tests for the pipe's transform method without any TestBed setup, verifying edge cases (empty string, limit longer than input)
